newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Highlands revises accounting policy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Highlands revises accounting policy.

text.p: Papua New Guinea gold miner Highlands Gold Ltd said it had changed its accounting policy to reflect the company's new direction and provide a sound base from which it could pursue its strategic objectives.

"The changes in accounting policies, which were adopted retrospectively, had a significant impact on the reported value of non current assets and on earnings for the year," the company said in a statement.
Earlier Highlands said it recorded a net loss of 11 million kina for the year to June 30, compared with a profit of 7.7 million kina in the previous year. (1.00 kina = US$0.765).

Highlands said it had adopted the units of production method of depreciation which resulted in the written down value of its assets at the Porgera gold mine in Paua New Guinea (PNG) being reduced to 60.6 million kina.
"The resulting lower carrying value for Porgera is considered by the board to be reasonable," the company said.
The company said its reported value of the long term receivable from the sale of a five percent interest in Porgera to the PNG government had been discounted to a present value.
"As a result, interest income of 1.8 million kina is brought to account in the 1995/96 year," Highlands said.
Porgera is owned equally by Highlands, the PNG government, Placer Pacific Ltd and Goldfields Ltd.

The PNG government increased its stake to 25 percent from 10 percent by a March 1993 agreement to acquire five percentage points each from the other three shareholders but has yet to pay for the shares.
Highlands said its 1995/96 earnings were also adversely impacted by lower gold production and higher costs at Porgera despite a higher realised gold price.
Earlier this year, MIM Holdings Ltd sold its 65 percent stake in Highlands through a rights issue to its own shareholders.
In July, Highlands said it would carry out bankable feasibility studies for the Freida-Nena copper-gold and the Ramu nickel-cobalt projects in Papua New Guinea.
Highlands shares closed one cent weaker at 54 cents.
